text: The story builds against mocks for the rwb-case case read, the CaseStateChanged message and the rwb-case reference-load of table DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST, keeps the legacy item names DocumentChecklist and the endpoints of TSD P5 API-P5-008 with a repeatable caseId query for the batch count, and runs the checklist refresh as the activity checklistRefresh on queue rwb-document inside the JOB-12 intake Schedule.
why: RWB-E1-040 is a moved story, so its behaviour and values are carried unchanged, while the case read, the reference load and the batch count have no operation ID or field names in any source, and the refresh step has no Schedule ID.
read: TSD P5 Document hub v2 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; legacy story RWB-E1-040 sections 4, 12 and 13; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11, DP-13 and R9
confirm: Solution architect publishes the rwb-case read, the reference load, the batch count and the Schedule ID before the wave-1 contract tests
impact: No build blocker: the service builds and tests against the mocks; a published name changes the contract tables and the fake, not the behaviour.

text: The checklist rows of version CHK-2026.11 and the approval of every load are carried from the legacy story as they stand, with the approval right A exercised by the legal counsel as co-owner of the checklist until the permission matrix grants it.
why: The legacy story fixes the items for LITIGATION and DEED_IN_LIEU and records that they are assumed until the bank list is signed (DL19), and that no role holds Reference data A today (DL01); the story cannot invent the signed list or the approver.
read: Legacy story RWB-E1-040 sections 3, 10 and 13; FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.16.3.3; Decision Log v10 DL01 and DL19
confirm: Legal counsel confirms the bank checklist and the approver role holds Reference data A
impact: A signed checklist or a new approver arrives as a new table version with a valid-from date; no code change and no story rework.

text: The checklist table is held and loaded as reference data owned by rwb-case under the default ruling of R3, while its rows live in document_checklist_item in rwb_document; the load is submitted and approved through the rwb-case reference-data contract and this service validates the rows.
why: R3 assigns parameters and reference data to P3 rwb-case, DP-07 sends reference data through the rwb-case contract, and the Ownership Map keeps document_checklist_item in P5; without the ruling the load would have two owners.
read: Template and Rules v1 R3 default rulings; R5.5 DP-07; context pack P5 ownership rows (document_checklist_item, case_document_check); TSD P5 appendix T-A
confirm: Architecture owner confirms the split of load ownership (P3) and row ownership (P5)
impact: One change process for the checklist; a move of the load to P5 would change section 3 and table 12.2 only.

text: The Quartz step checklistRefreshStep of JOB-12 becomes the activity checklistRefresh of the JOB-12 intake Schedule on queue rwb-document, at the same every-15-minute cadence, through the workflow kit of RWB-PLT-E1071-CON.
why: DP-10 replaces Quartz and JOB-nn with a Temporal Schedule or an event-started workflow, and the legacy story holds the refresh as one step of JOB-12; the sources name no Schedule and no separate refresh job.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-10; legacy story RWB-E1-040 flow step 8 and section 13; FSD P5 AC-BG-P5-016-01 (document intake, every 15 minutes)
confirm: RWB-PLT-E1071-CON fixes the Schedule definitions and the activity contract
impact: The refresh runs inside an existing Schedule; if a Schedule of its own is required, only the Schedule row of section 12.6 changes.
